concerns.text: FR-001 (and FR-002, FR-003, FR-004, FR-005, FR-006, FR-007) reference “(See US-1)”, “(See US-2)”, “(See US-3)” but no identifiers US-1/US-2/US-3 are defined; the user stories are titled “User Story 1”, “User Story 2”, etc.
Inconsistent terminology: the spec calls the narratives “User Story 1”, “User Story 2”, … but elsewhere they are referenced as US‑1, US‑2, US‑3. This creates ambiguity for traceability.
SC‑001 specifies a flag based on Pearson’s r > 0.3, yet FR‑003 states the system computes Spearman rank correlation (rho). The success criterion and functional requirement are mismatched.

SC‑003 requires measuring the validity of demographic controls by comparing regression coefficients with and without covariates, but the specification (FR‑004 and User Story 2) only describes a single regression model that includes the covariates; no baseline‑only model is defined.

Constitution Principle VI mandates Pearson correlations and Bonferroni correction, while the spec (FR‑003, FR‑005) prescribes Spearman correlations and Benjamini‑Hochberg FDR correction, directly violating a non‑negotiable statistical‑transparency rule.
